t: You're looking at 2 to 11 Gloucester Gate and its attached railings, a Grade I listed terrace of residential buildings on the edge of Regent's Park. It was designed by John Nash, the architect of the Georgian and Regency eras who shaped many important parts of London in the neoclassical and picturesque styles. His designs were financed by the Prince Regent and by the property developer James Burton, and he worked closely with Burton's son, Decimus Burton.
